howto.name: Add your images
howto.text: Drop or select the pictures for the collage. They fill the grid left to right, top to bottom.

howto.name: Arrange the tiles
howto.text: Drag the thumbnails to change their order. What you see in the preview is the order the finished collage uses.

howto.name: Choose the grid
howto.text: By default the tool finds a balanced, roughly square grid for the number of images, up to six columns. Switch that off to set the columns yourself, anywhere from 1 to 6.

howto.name: Adjust spacing and background
howto.text: Spacing between the tiles runs from 0 to 100 pixels and starts at 10. The background colour shows through that gap and around the edges, and starts as white.

howto.name: Build and download
howto.text: Create the collage and save the single combined image.

faq.a: In a grid, filled left to right and top to bottom. The automatic setting picks a near-square layout; set the columns yourself for a different shape — one column for a vertical strip, or a high number for a wide banner.

faq.q: Do the pictures need to be the same size?
faq.a: No, but a set of similar shapes produces a tidier grid. Mixing portrait and landscape shots leaves uneven tiles, so resizing them to a common size first with Resize and Crop Image gives a cleaner result.

faq.q: What does the spacing setting do?
faq.a: It sets the gap between tiles in pixels, from none at all up to 100. Zero produces a seamless block; a wider gap with a contrasting background colour gives the framed, scrapbook look.

faq.q: Can I change the background colour?
faq.a: Yes. It defaults to white and shows in the gaps and borders. Black or a brand colour makes a set of photographs look deliberate rather than accidental.
Yes. Drag the thumbnails in the preview to reorder them before you build the collage; the finished image follows that order.
A single image containing the whole grid, which you can then treat like any other picture — compress it, resize it, or add a watermark.

faq.q: What happens to my images after I upload them?
faq.a: It is uploaded over HTTPS and converted on the PrivaTools server using local imaging libraries, not a third-party conversion service. The file sits in isolated temporary per-request storage while it is read; response cleanup removes the input and the output once your download has been sent, and a background sweep clears anything an interrupted request leaves behind.
